caption:
Always saying "I'm good" at work when you're not? 👇

Someone asks how you're doing. "I'm good, man." You're not. You haven't been in months.

That act costs energy. Every "I'm good" is weight you carry all shift, so you get home with nothing left.

You're not alone. In Monster's 2026 State of Workplace Mental Health Report, 7 in 10 U.S. workers said they feel pressure to appear "okay" at work.

The fix: drop the act a little. Swap "I'm good" for "Long week, but I'm still standing." Honest, safe, and lighter to carry.

You don't have to be fine. You just have to be honest.

When did YOU last tell someone how you really are? 👇

slides.big: I hate to break it to you, but they're probably never going to say thank you.
slides.small: So stop waiting for it to keep you going.

You cover the extra shift.
You fix the thing nobody else could.
Nobody says a word.
But the one mistake? Everyone hears about that.

You're not tired of the work.
You're tired of nobody noticing it.
Feeling invisible wears a man down.
In DHR Global's 2026 Workforce Trends Report, workers naming lack of reward or recognition as a top cause of burnout nearly doubled, from 17% to 32%.

Open the notes app on your phone.
At the end of each shift, write 3 things you got done.
Read the list every Friday.
Now there's proof, even if nobody else says it.

slides.big:
They may never see it.
You can.

caption:
Work hard every day and nobody ever says thank you? 👇

You cover the extra shift. You fix what nobody else could. Nobody says a word. But one mistake, and everyone hears about it.

You're not tired of the work. You're tired of nobody noticing it.

It's not just you. In DHR Global's 2026 Workforce Trends Report, workers naming lack of reward or recognition as a top burnout cause nearly doubled, from 17% to 32%.

The fix: notice it yourself. At the end of each shift, write 3 things you got done in your phone's notes. Read the list every Friday.

They may never see it. You can.

What's ONE thing you did this week nobody noticed? 👇
